OpenPoke
nodes.description: Fork addressing Execution Agent Overload; retains Interaction Agent and Execution Agent architecture.

nodes.label: Interaction Agent
nodes.description: User-facing agent that delegates work to Execution Agents; discovery exposes at most 30 compact candidates per turn, ten at a time.

nodes.label: Execution Agents
nodes.description: Persistent saved work delegated by the Interaction Agent; task state and original records support continuity.

nodes.label: Execution Agent Overload
nodes.description: Overload comprises finding relevant work, loading useful memory, and controlling concurrent work.
nodes.rationale: A full growing agent roster and histories consumed unrelated context while execution lacked a shared concurrency limit.

nodes.label: Proposed screenshot comparison
nodes.description: Proposed before-and-after comparison of the same request and saved work using chat, selected agent, candidate counts, and context size.
nodes.rationale: Pair visible chat behavior with automated evidence; the README explicitly says this demo is proposed and is not a completed test.

nodes.label: Reported November 14 offline results
nodes.description: README reports 129 passing tests, 100% recall@30 on 60 cases, and candidate pools bounded at 30 for 1,000/10,000 agents.
nodes.rationale: Deterministic embeddings validate mechanics; these results do not establish live model selection or real Gmail workflow success.

nodes.label: Agent overload optimization
nodes.description: Implementation documentation covering retrieval, storage, queueing, recovery, lifecycle, and verification.

nodes.label: Routing and identity
nodes.description: Resolve stable IDs and conversation links first; otherwise search, compare compact descriptions, inspect current records, and then dispatch.
nodes.rationale: Contacts and email threads may belong to multiple tasks; conflicting confirmed task-specific identifiers exclude a candidate.

nodes.label: Hybrid registry search
nodes.description: Keyword and semantic rankings each contribute 30 candidates; reciprocal rank fusion uses k=60. OpenRouter embeddings use openai/text-embedding-3-small; cached NumPy exact cosine search ranks normalized float32 vectors.

nodes.label: Stable task identity
nodes.description: Display-name changes preserve task identity; legacy aliases retain trigger ownership, and colliding legacy history names remain ambiguous.

nodes.label: Scoped task references
nodes.description: Search yields observed references; confirm_task_reference promotes a task-specific identifier only when supported by a cited task tool result.
nodes.rationale: Model-generated metadata alone is not trusted provenance.

nodes.label: SQLite registry.db
nodes.description: Default server/data/agents/registry.db stores registry records, scoped references, FTS5, vectors/index work, source events/artifacts, summaries, jobs/batches, and interaction journals. FTS5 support is required.

nodes.label: Source events and artifacts
nodes.description: New executions preserve complete structured arguments/results; scoped artifact and source cursors retrieve large results. Legacy truncation cannot be recovered.

nodes.label: Bounded execution context
nodes.description: Execution context combines task state, earlier-work summary, and recent complete request segments; source records survive compaction.
nodes.rationale: Keep prompts bounded while retaining original evidence for exact details; conservative token estimates are not exact provider guarantees.

nodes.label: Shared persistent execution queue
nodes.description: Chat and trigger executions share configurable defaults: four concurrent executions, 100 queued jobs, five-minute queue wait, 300-second execution deadline, and one running execution per task. One backend process is supported.

nodes.label: Sealed result groups
nodes.description: Batch membership persists at submission; groups deliver only after the initiating interaction seals them and every member is terminal. Follow-up defaults allow five stages and 20 submissions.

nodes.label: Interrupted execution review
nodes.description: Tool-journal evidence classifies interruptions. Attempted writes or unknown tools require review; blocked submissions expose the blocking execution ID.
nodes.rationale: An external action may already have happened, so OpenPoke does not automatically repeat uncertain effects.

nodes.label: One automatic read-only retry
nodes.description: A request permits at most one automatic retry of safe interrupted read-only work; its source execution is durable. Blocked, expired, rejected, or uncertain work is not automatically retried.
nodes.rationale: Persisted retry provenance prevents another delivery or replacement agent from resetting the allowance.

nodes.label: Durable interaction journal
nodes.description: Interaction responses and tool-call plans persist before effects; stable operation/event keys make recovery resume committed steps.

nodes.label: Deduplicated reminder occurrences
nodes.description: Occurrences deduplicate by trigger ID, scheduled time, and reset generation; schedule advancement projects durable outcomes idempotently. Interrupted occurrences are not replayed.

nodes.label: Reset generation fencing
nodes.description: History reset quiesces interactions, queue, indexing, compaction, reminders, and watchers before advancing generation; late callbacks cannot recreate cleared state.

nodes.label: Explicit task lifecycle
nodes.description: States are open, waiting_for_user, waiting_for_trigger, completed, and needs_review. report_task_state declares goal state; successful invocation alone is not task completion.

nodes.label: Protected automatic archival
nodes.description: Startup/hourly maintenance archives explicitly completed tasks after 30 inactive days. Work, reminders, approval, ambiguous legacy history, and unresolved interruptions protect tasks; archives remain searchable.
nodes.rationale: Inactivity alone does not establish completion; accepted continuation reopens saved work.

nodes.label: Independent rollout controls
nodes.description: OPENPOKE_AGENT_HYBRID_SEARCH, OPENPOKE_AGENT_COMPACTION, and OPENPOKE_AGENT_AUTO_ARCHIVE each default to 1 and can be disabled independently.

nodes.label: Chat request idempotency
nodes.description: Optional Idempotency-Key on /chat/send deduplicates retries; successful admission returns empty HTTP 202 and X-Request-ID. Different content under the same key returns 409; reset admission returns 503.

nodes.label: Retrieval evaluator
nodes.description: tests/evaluation/evaluate_agent_retrieval.py evaluates 60 labeled cases and 1,000/10,000-agent benchmarks. Offline synonym-aware deterministic embeddings measure retrieval mechanics.

nodes.label: Solution board and sequence guide
nodes.description: Guide to the editable solution board and sequence source.

nodes.label: Agent overload solution board
nodes.description: Editable Excalidraw board with ten independent cards grouped as Find and reuse work, Keep context useful, and Run and maintain work.
nodes.rationale: Cards explain problem, change, and why it helps; the board reports existing offline evidence and did not rerun tests.

nodes.label: Next.js frontend

nodes.label: Execution Agent instructions
nodes.description: System prompt instructing Poke's execution engine to complete delegated goals and return results through Poke.

nodes.label: Draft confirmation requirement
nodes.description: Create a draft before sending; execute it only after explicit confirmation. Return exact recipient, subject, and body to the Interaction Agent.
nodes.rationale: Preparing a draft does not authorize sending an email.

nodes.label: Execution Gmail tools
nodes.description: Prompt lists gmail_create_draft, gmail_execute_draft, gmail_forward_email, and gmail_reply_to_thread.

nodes.label: Reminder trigger tools
nodes.description: Prompt lists createTrigger, updateTrigger, and listTriggers; schedules require explicit ISO 8601 start_time and recurrence RRULE in the detected user timezone.

nodes.label: Exact source evidence
nodes.description: Use read_agent_history for missing exact details and cite source event IDs with confirm_task_reference; never infer absent legacy details.
nodes.rationale: Search hits are observed evidence rather than established task identity.

nodes.label: report_task_state
nodes.description: Call before final response; drafts awaiting review imply waiting_for_user, enabled reminders imply waiting_for_trigger, and completed requires the actual goal to be finished.

nodes.label: Interaction Agent instructions
nodes.description: System prompt for OpenPoke user communication, saved-task routing, asynchronous execution, and approvals.

nodes.label: new_user_message
nodes.description: Only this field represents a new human instruction.

nodes.label: new_agent_message
nodes.description: Execution results or background notifications do not provide fresh user authorization.

nodes.label: Reuse saved work
nodes.description: Continue matching saved tasks; resolve explicit references first, search archives, inspect ambiguous candidates, and create only after archive-inclusive discovery.
nodes.rationale: Parallel scheduling is not a reason to duplicate task histories; similarity alone does not prove identity.

nodes.label: Version-checked task dispatch
nodes.description: Inspect before send_message_to_agent and pass immutable agent_id plus current version; inspect again if state changed.
nodes.rationale: Display names are not stable identity and stale records cannot justify dispatch.

nodes.label: User-directed interruption resolution
nodes.description: Resolving uncertain external work requires direct user instruction to complete, abandon, or retry; do not autonomously repeat uncertain actions.
nodes.rationale: Background notifications and uncertain outcomes do not provide authorization for repeated effects.

nodes.label: Asynchronous execution results
nodes.description: Submitted or queued work is not completed work; outcomes are grouped by initiating request and include failures, expiration, and interruptions.

nodes.label: send_draft
nodes.description: Present exact draft recipient, subject, body, and related agent_id; separately ask the user how to proceed.

nodes.label: Agent overload: the solutions
nodes.rationale: The image is an interview walkthrough board with one fix per card, grouped into three solution categories. It presents design decisions and recorded claims, not independently verified runtime implementation.

nodes.label: Agent overload
nodes.rationale: The problem banner says growing saved tasks and histories expose the model to irrelevant context and allow too much simultaneous work. The proposed response bounds what the model sees, what each worker remembers, and how much work runs. These are diagram claims, not verified runtime behavior.

nodes.label: Find and reuse work
nodes.rationale: The purple column proposes keeping discovery relevant as saved tasks grow. Its visual grouping describes a design category and does not verify that runtime discovery follows it.

nodes.label: Keep context useful
nodes.rationale: The blue column proposes small prompts while preserving access to original details. Its visual grouping describes a design category and does not verify runtime context management.

nodes.label: Run and maintain work
nodes.rationale: The green column proposes bounded execution and preserved task continuity. Its visual grouping describes a design category and does not verify runtime scheduling or maintenance.

nodes.label: Search instead of loading the roster
nodes.rationale: Card 01 proposes saved task links or keyword plus semantic search, showing at most 30 compact candidates in pages of 10 while retaining the directory in storage. The design intent is relevant discovery instead of carrying every saved agent name; implementation and runtime limits are not verified by this image.

nodes.label: Check identity before continuing
nodes.rationale: Card 02 proposes inspecting the current saved record and stable task ID and rejecting conflicting confirmed invoice or case IDs. The design avoids continuing a different task for the same person, illustrated by INV-1042 versus INV-1043; runtime enforcement is not verified by this image.

nodes.label: Reuse work before creating more
nodes.rationale: Card 03 proposes searching active and archived work before creation and continuing a verified match under its existing ID. The design aims to preserve task history and reduce duplicate agents; runtime reuse is not verified by this image.

nodes.label: Bound the conversation context
nodes.rationale: Card 04 proposes budgeted Interaction Agent conversation memory and recent saved task links to keep growing chats manageable while retaining continuation links. These are design claims, not verified runtime memory behavior.

nodes.label: Load a compact task memory
nodes.rationale: Card 05 proposes loading structured task state, an earlier-work summary, and recent history within a fixed budget. It describes token counts as estimates with a safety margin. The intended result is bounded working context as history grows; runtime budgeting is not verified by this image.

nodes.label: Retrieve exact details on demand
nodes.rationale: Card 06 proposes preserving new tool results as full source records and retrieving original events or large-result excerpts when a summary omits exact details. The design avoids placing every original record in the prompt; runtime preservation and retrieval are not verified by this image.

nodes.label: Put all executions in one queue
nodes.rationale: Card 07 proposes a persistent queue shared by chat and triggers, with defaults of 4 running, 100 waiting, and at most 1 run per task. The design bounds active work and prevents concurrent updates to the same saved task; runtime queue behavior is not verified by this image.

nodes.label: Limit stalls and recover safely
nodes.rationale: Card 08 proposes a 300-second run deadline, resuming unexpired queued jobs, one automatic safe read-only retry per request, and review of uncertain writes. The design releases stuck workers while avoiding blind repetition of uncertain actions; runtime recovery behavior is not verified by this image.

nodes.label: Return related results together
nodes.rationale: Card 09 proposes saving each request's result group and delivering it after the group is sealed and every job is terminal, including failed or rejected jobs. It also lists defaults of 5 follow-up stages and 20 submissions. The design groups related outcomes; runtime delivery behavior is not verified by this image.

nodes.label: Archive completed work safely
nodes.rationale: Card 10 proposes archiving explicitly completed tasks after 30 inactive days, while pending work, approvals, and active triggers prevent automatic archival. Archived tasks remain searchable and can reopen for continuation. The design reduces active-list clutter; runtime archival behavior is not verified by this image.

nodes.label: Evidence and practical limits
nodes.rationale: The board reports recorded offline results dated November 14, 2026 and explicitly says tests were not rerun for this board: 129 automated tests passed, 100% recall@30 across 60 labeled retrieval cases, no identity-conflict or ambiguity-guard failures, and candidate pools of 30 with 1,000 and 10,000 saved agents. It also says offline embeddings and model/Gmail behavior are test doubles, candidate recall does not establish correct live model choice or real Gmail success, live end-to-end testing remains necessary, and one backend process is supported. These are documented evidence claims and limitations, not independent runtime verification.
